basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 2.' and it opens '(Vers. 2.) Et Spiritus Dei ferebatur super aquas. Pro eo quod in nostris codicibus'. The printing's caput is stale here, its marker for this chapter being missing, so the chapter is taken from the lemma, whose best match anywhere in Genesis falls on the very verse the printing numbers.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 2.) Et Spiritus Dei ferebatur super aquas. Pro eo quod in nostris codicibus scriptum est, ferebatur, in Hebraeo habet MEREFETH (מרחפת), quod nos appellare possumus, incubabat, sive confovebat, in similitudinem volucris, ova calore animantis. Ex quo intelligimus, non de spiritu mundi dici, ut nonnulli arbitrantur, sed de Spiritu Sancto, qui et ipse vivificator omnium a principio dicitur. Si autem vivificator, consequenter et conditor. Quod si conditor, et Deus. Emitte enim, ait, Spiritum tuum, et creabuntur (Psal. CIII, 30).
